assumptions: The +0x18/+0x10 links form a tree; a cyclic graph would not terminate in the binary either, so the model raises instead of looping.
The source-level names and kinds of the node, its +0x40 member and the tree itself are not pinned; only field offsets and the transition rules are.
The 0x5d35c30 callee is used call-shape only; its allocation behaviour is not modelled.
The string size field at +0x28 is never read by this routine; only the pointer at +0x20 and the capacity at +0x30 decide disposal in the manual idiom.
No reason for the compiler's manual versus _M_dispose idiom split is claimed; only the observed level boundary (manual at frame levels 0-4, _M_dispose at frame levels 5-8) is pinned.

distinction.deep_tree_teardown_55d50: 0x50-byte nodes, string at +0x20, refcounted payload at +0x48 released through 0x5d350c0
distinction.node_tree_teardown_55aa0: 0x38-byte nodes, refcounted payload at +0x30 released through 0x5d350c0, no string
distinction.this_routine: 0x58-byte nodes, string at +0x20, unconditional 0x5d35c30 call on the +0x40 member

exits.condition: null root at entry, or the root chain is exhausted

exits.form: the routine never returns early; each node's teardown ends in its sized delete and the chain walk continues

node.first_child: node +0x18, whole subtree destroyed before the node
node.next_sibling: node +0x10, read before the node is freed, followed after the node is destroyed

recursion.rule: a node at absolute depth d is disposed with the idiom of frame level d mod 9 (manual when 0-4, _M_dispose when 5-8), because the self-recursion restarts the frame
recursion.self_call_argument: the level-8 node's +0x18 child, as the new root

manual.rule: if [node+0x20] equals node+0x30, nothing is freed; otherwise sized delete ([node+0x20], [node+0x30] + 1)

teardown_order: dispose the +0x20 string with the frame-level idiom
sized-delete the node with size 0x58 through _ZdlPvm PLT 0x63f0d80
traversal: post-order: for each node in the +0x10 chain starting at the root, destroy its +0x18 subtree first, then tear the node down, then move to the next +0x10 node; a null child link jumps straight to the parent level's dispose block; each dispose block follows the freed node's +0x10 link
